title: Finite-level mapping-complex duality
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use ordinary module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, with completed coefficient sheaf $R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ for $W=X,s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $F_n=Ra_{!,n}$ for compact support using one fixed compactification $a=pj$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], $G_n=Ra_n^!$ for the finite constructible comparison-class exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and $\omega_n=G_n(A_n)_s$. For $n\ge1$ let $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ be constructible [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] with finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and put $C_n(M)=\Gamma(s,F_nM)$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Global derived mapping complexes mean derived global sections of derived sheaf Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism in $D(A_n)$
$$\gamma_{n,M}:\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(M,\omega_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(C_n(M),A_n).$$
It is the transpose of compact-support projection followed by evaluation and the exceptional counit $F_n\omega_n\to(A_n)_s$. Under the finite site comparison [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison], it agrees with the ordinary etale internal exceptional adjunction [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] followed by global sections and the finite coefficient-point identification [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence].

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: At finite level the adjunction on derived mapping complexes follows by applying derived global sections to prop-asd-internal-adjunction on the etale site and transporting it by the finite site comparisons (old step 7).
